newsitem.title: UK: Med Aframaxes tankers shoot up, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Med Aframaxes tankers shoot up, others steady.

text.p: The Mediterranean Aframax (80,000 tonne) sector was the star of the dirty tanker market on Thursday, firming some 20 points from earlier in the week and 50 points over last week's levels, brokers said.
Cross-Med Aframaxes were pegged at W160, adding to the firm trend of the last couple of days on a lack of vessels, they added.
Among the vessels reported fixed at this level in the last 24 hours were the Armata on a Banias/Italy trip for KPC and the Zrinsky Banias/Med for Total.
"There are only one or two cargoes for June but there's a big shortage of ships," one broker said.
"Fixing for late in the month started quite early which implied a lot of activity and made owners bullish. We will see whether it lasts. It's very hard to tell," another added.
He also cited a tugboat strike at Fos near Marseille which has been preventing tankers from unloading oil bound for some of the region's biggest refineries.
U.K./Cont Aframaxes were firm at W125, up some 10-15 points from last week, but lacked the impetus to climb further for now, brokers said.
Oil traders said most North Sea cargoes in the first decade of July had already been snapped up, with prices firming.
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs), meanwhile, were quiet but steady with 250,000 tonne cargoes to Japan at W72.5.

The 237,000 tonne Tagawa Maru was fixed at W73.5 for Jomo, while the ultra-large sector, which was dead last week, showed further signs of revival with the 315,000 tonne Karoline done at W60 on a Kharg/Red Sea voyage for BP.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCC rates were also steady at W65, with Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) at W87.5.

Activity in the western hemisphere picked up, but rates refused to budge from W170 for 70,000 crude cargoes and W190 for 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems, brokers said. They attributed this to sufficient tonnage and no weather delays.
"I think dirty rates could slip over the next couple of months," predicted one U.S. broker.
In the inter-UKC sector, 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged down to W210, while Med rates were steady at W190. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
